newsitem.title: MEXICO: Some Unicom partners join Mexico's Alestra.
newsitem.headline: Some Unicom partners join Mexico's Alestra.

text.p: Mexican industrial conglomerate Grupo Industrial Alfa and its U.S. long-distance telecommunications partner AT&T on Tuesday announced the formal incorporation of former rivals Valores Industriales (Visa) and Bancomer into telephone firm Alestra.

The two latter firms, who formed joint venture Unicom to compete with Alestra, took a 25.4 percent shareholding in Alestra. Alfa now has 25.6 percent and AT&T 49 percent of the joint venture, which along with other firms will take part in long-distance phone competition in Mexico from next year.
Two other members of Unicom, Telefonica Internacional de Espana and GTE, did not join Alestra.
Alfa and AT&T said in a statement that Telefonica was still considering joining.
"GTE will not join Alestra at this time, but expects to resume discussions at a future time concerning its entry," the statement said.

Current long-distance monopoly holder Telefonos de Mexico faces full competition from Alestra, Avantel and other telephone firms from January 1 next year. Avantel is a joint venture between MCI of the United States and Grupo Financiero Banamex Accival of Mexico.
